html:
Shah of Safavid Iran from 1588 to 1629, the strongest ruler of his dynasty. He took back land lost to the Ottomans and Uzbeks and made Isfahan one of the grandest cities in the world.

He came to the throne at 16, with the realm torn by feuding tribes and invaded on two sides. He made peace with the Ottoman Empire at a high price, then built a new army loyal only to him: slave soldiers taken from Georgians, Armenians and Circassians, with musketeers and cannon. With it he retook Khorasan from the Uzbeks and then Tabriz and later Baghdad from the Ottomans. In 1622, with help from ships of the East India Company, he took the island of Hormuz from Portugal.

He moved his capital to Isfahan and built the vast square of Naqsh-e Jahan, with the Shah Mosque, palaces and bazaars around it. He deported thousands of Armenians from Julfa to a new suburb, New Julfa, to run the silk trade, the base of networks such as Hovhannes's trading journey. He was also cruel and suspicious, killing or blinding his own sons, which left weak heirs.
sum: Shah of Safavid Iran from 1588 to 1629, the strongest ruler of his dynasty. He took back land lost to the Ottomans and Uzbeks and made Isfahan one of the grandest cities in the world.
